$comment: PRODUCT-INTENT CONFIRMATION RECORD. Two field groups are deliberately kept separate and must never be merged: (1) intended_asin / official_listing_url / confirmation_date / confirmation_source describe what the submitter INTENDED; (2) observed_redirect_* describe what a fetch actually returned. An observation is not a confirmation of intent. Amazon's own ASIN definition is the checkable identifier, so a mapping only becomes 'confirmed' when the owner states the ASIN or when a dated Associates report shows the click landing on that ASIN.

field_rules.intended_asin: Set only from a statement by the link submitter or from an Associates tracking report. Never inferred from a redirect. Null when unknown.
field_rules.official_listing_url: Canonical https://www.amazon.com/dp/<ASIN> built from intended_asin only. Null when intended_asin is null.
field_rules.confirmation_date: ISO date the intent was confirmed. Null when unconfirmed.
field_rules.confirmation_source: What confirmed it (person, message, report id). Null when unconfirmed.
field_rules.observed_redirect_target: Exact URL the short link resolved to during automated observation. Evidence only. Never copied into intended_asin.
field_rules.observation_method: How the observation was made, so it can be repeated.

Automated fetch returned an Amazon bot-check interstitial (/checkpoint/continue), then the Amazon homepage on retry. A direct ASIN-page fetch for B0C8MOW59 returned no result. Repeated attempts produced the same two outcomes.
